title: Bundle Size & Build Optimizations 📦
description: Reduce initial load time with production builds, tree‑shaking, lazy loading, and budgets.

slides.title: Why Bundle Size Matters ⏱️
slides.content:
# First Impressions Count

Users expect apps to load in under 2 seconds. Every kilobyte of JavaScript adds download, parse, and execution time.

Angular provides several built‑in mechanisms to keep your app lean:
* **Production mode** – disables assertions and debug tools.
* **Tree‑shaking** – removes unused code.
* **Lazy loading** – loads modules only when needed.
* **AOT compilation** – pre‑compiles templates ahead of time.
* **Budget thresholds** – warn or error if bundles exceed a limit.

slides.title: Production Build with AOT
slides.content: Always use the production configuration for deployment:

slides.title: AOT Compilation & Ivy 🌿
slides.content:
Angular's **Ivy** renderer (default since v9) compiles templates during the build process (Ahead‑Of‑Time) rather than in the browser.

Benefits:
* Faster rendering (no runtime compiler).
* Smaller bundle size (the compiler is not shipped).
* Better template error detection at build time.

In production mode, AOT is enabled by default.

quizData.question: Angular's production build uses AOT compilation by default, which reduces bundle size and improves runtime performance.
quizData.explanation: AOT compiles templates during the build, removing the need for the Angular compiler in the browser bundle.

slides.title: Lazy Loading & Preloading (Review) 🔄
slides.content:
As seen in Chapter 5, lazy loading splits the app into chunks. Use it for all feature modules.

Preloading strategies (`PreloadAllModules` or custom) load lazy chunks in the background after the initial app is ready, giving instant navigation.

```typescript
RouterModule.forRoot(routes, { preloadingStrategy: PreloadAllModules })
```

slides.title: Configuring Budgets
slides.content: Set size budgets in `angular.json` to catch bloat early:

slides.title: Differential Loading 🚛
slides.content:
Angular automatically generates separate bundles for modern browsers (ES2015+) and legacy browsers (ES5). Modern browsers get smaller, faster code.

This is called **differential loading** and is enabled by default for production builds.

quizData.question: To set a maximum warning size for the initial bundle, you configure ________ in angular.json.
quizData.explanation: Budgets in angular.json define size thresholds that warn or error during build.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Analyze Your Bundle

Run `ng build --stats-json` and then use tools like `webpack‑bundle‑analyzer` or `source‑map‑explorer` to see exactly what's making your bundle large.
